ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended, incl. 2011 Amendment and economic substance provisions); International Companies Regulations 1998; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2007; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Regulations 2009 (as amended 2018); SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines and Customer Due Diligence (CDD) Guidance Notes; applicable United Nations Sanctions Regulations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — beneficial ownership records are maintained privately by the SIFA-licensed registered agent at the statutory registered office; the register of members and UBO records are not publicly searchable. Access is limited to the Registrar of International Companies, the Samoa International Finance Authority, the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, and foreign competent authorities exclusively via Mutual Legal Assistance / Tax Information Exchange channels. No public UBO register exists for International Companies.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs (25% and above), directors, secretary and the licensed registered agent against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the OFAC SDN List; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) the UK OFSI Consolidated List; and (v) domestic designated-person lists maintained by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit. PEP identification applies per FATF standards, with mandatory enhanced due diligence for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, or UBOs holding 10% or more in a corporate chain. Each corporate shareholder must be pierced to the ultimate natural person; all intermediate UBO registers are collected until the 25% natural-person threshold is fully satisfied. Suspicious transaction reports are filed with the Samoa FIU; CDD and transaction records must be retained for at least 5 years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — International Companies Registry; name reservation submitted electronically via the SIFA e-Services portal (www.sifa.ws) through a licensed registered agent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be expressed in English (Latin/Roman script). Samoan alphabet characters are permissible but not required. Chinese characters are not permitted in the statutory registered name; however, because this entity supports a fully bilingual governance model for Greater China founders, the Articles of Association may be executed bilingually in Chinese and English (English controlling version lodged with SIFA), and a Chinese trading name may be used as a secondary marketing/banking name. The name must end with a recognized suffix: 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Public Limited Company' or abbreviations 'Ltd', 'Corp', 'Inc', 'P.L.C'. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any registered Samoa or International Company, any reserved name, and must not imply a connection with the Samoan Government.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days by written application to SIFA through the licensed registered agent with payment of the applicable extension fee. Upon rejection, the applicant may: (1) submit a formal written reconsideration request to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, attaching supporting evidence; (2) if rejected again, file a ministerial appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days; (3) if the refusal is caused by a sensitive or prohibited token, obtain the prior written consent of the Central Bank of Samoa or the relevant Ministerial authority and re-file a fresh name reservation; (4) if the name conflicts with a similarly registered name, submit a written consent letter from the prior name holder; (5) final recourse is judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is NOT acceptable as the statutory registered office. Under the International Companies Act 1987, the company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa (typically Apia) at the premises of a SIFA-licensed registered agent / international company service provider. The company's actual software, ERP/CRM development and cloud operations may be conducted entirely remotely and offshore; Samoan commercial substance is limited to the registered agent, registered office, statutory registers, and any applicable economic substance filing. The registered agent's address serves as the legal seat for service of process and statutory records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: LOW (estimated 10–20% probability within the first operating year). SIFA conducts risk-tiered, unannounced AML/CFT supervisory inspections of licensed registered agents; for a Low_Risk_Standard vertical cloud software company with no statutory license requirement, targeted inspection of the end-client is unlikely, but the company must maintain current registers of directors, members and UBOs, minutes, and financial records at the registered office and must respond to SIFA's compliance questionnaire within 10 business days if requested.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 5-7 (incorporation), s. 24 (registered office), ss. 36-44 (officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Application for Incorporation Form IC-1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit. The Memorandum may declare authorized share capital as set by the subscriber; shares may be issued for consideration as determined by the board.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the Board of Directors of [Company Name] (the Company), in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as follows: (1) The subscription by the sole subscriber for 1,000 shares of US$1.00 each, as set out in the Memorandum and Articles, is hereby ratified and approved. (2) The registered office is established at the licensed registered agent's office in Apia, Samoa, and the registered agent is authorized to accept service of process. (3) [Name] is appointed first director, [Name] is appointed secretary, and [Name] is appointed principal officer, each with full authority to open bank accounts and execute documents. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Registry, MCIL - name reservation desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via a licensed Samoa registered agent or the MCIL online portal. The proposed name must end with 'Limited' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing company or contain words restricted by the International Companies Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an alternative name or file a written application for reconsideration through the registered agent, providing evidence of distinctiveness and lawful usage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent and notary public in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, setting out the corporate name, share capital, registered office clause and object clause for vertical enterprise software and cloud CRM services. Have the subscriber sign the document in the presence of a notary; obtain notarization of the signature page and consent of the first director and secretary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a substantive or formal deficiency, amend the constitutional document and re-execute it, or file a corrective affidavit and supporting exhibits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application and government fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Registry, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles, the name reservation certificate, and the registered agent/registered office consent. Pay the non-refundable filing fee of USD 350 via licensed agent remittance or registry-approved online payment gateway.
required_dossiers: Registered agent and registered office consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, address the Registrar's objections within 14 days by filing revised documents; if rejected, request reconsideration or appeal to the Minister responsible for international financial services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and filing of officer details
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Registry, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation containing the company number and date of incorporation. Verify that all corporate details are correct, then file the notice of first director and officer and the office notification with the Registry. Obtain the company seal and corporate minute book from the registered agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For typographical errors or omissions, submit Form IC-5 (Change/Rectification) and obtain a certificate of rectification from the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolution and banking onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution (written resolution) approving share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments. With this corporate kit, open a corporate bank account, providing certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, the resolution, and identity documents of the beneficial owner and appointees.
required_dossiers: Passport copies and proof of residential address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank requires additional due diligence, provide a registered agent confirmation letter, corporate diagram, and apostilled or notarized copies to remedy the deficiency.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial licensing board mandate for an offshore International Company; if a domestic physical presence were established, the Business Licence Registry under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour would apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - no statutory operating or manufacturing permit applies to a cloud software vertical ERP/CRM company under the International Companies Act 1987.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the proposed offshore software services entity involves no physical development, construction, or industrial activity requiring an EIA under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A - no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated by a non-physical cloud licensing operation; software services are conducted remotely through third-party data centers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for an offshore company with no physical occupation in Samoa. Should a branch back office be opened, fire safety certification from the Fire and Emergency Services Authority and a building occupancy inspection under the Samoa National Building Code would be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) - official portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) by applying to the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) either online through the SRA e-Services portal or by lodged Form TIN-01, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office certificate, and proof of identity and address of directors and shareholders. International Companies are registered under the International Companies Act 2008 and enjoy income tax exemption; the TIN is issued for administrative and VAT purposes only if the entity makes taxable supplies. A separate VAGST registration (Form VAT-01) is required once the annual turnover from local taxable supplies exceeds WST 47,000.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a check-the-box classification election for tax purposes. An International Company may elect to convert to a local company under the Companies Act 2001, thereby subjecting itself to ordinary income tax; may voluntarily elect for VAGST registration if below threshold; and may elect to claim zero-rating for exported supplies through the return. Hybrid mismatch election mechanisms are not available under Samoa law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Samoa Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 47,000 annual taxable turnover (voluntary registration below threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory API-based e-invoicing system is in force. Suppliers must issue a valid VAGST tax invoice for taxable supplies, including electronically generated invoices, but no digital stamping approval is required. The Ministry of Revenue operates a receipted cash-register mandate only for prescribed retail/hospitality activities; vertical cloud software B2B exports are outside that scope.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available on exports of goods where physical export from Samoa is proven by customs documentation. For services, including vertical ERP/CRM cloud software, a supply is zero-rated when provided to a non-resident who is outside Samoa and the services are used wholly outside Samoa. The supplier must retain evidence of the non-resident status, place of consumption, and export contract.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or air waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank foreign exchange record
External service agreement or cloud licensing/use-right contract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SRA conducts risk-based audits of zero-rated claims; failure to substantiate eligibility results in VAGST clawback plus interest and a shortfall penalty of up to 100% of the tax; intentional evasion carries a further 100% civil penalty and criminal liability with fines up to WST 500,000 and/or imprisonment for up to five years. Directors of International Companies are jointly and severally liable for fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) acting under the Exchange Control Act 1970, the International Companies Act 1987, and the National Payments System Act 2016; the CBS is the sole foreign exchange administration authority in Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa maintains a managed-float exchange control regime; the Samoan tala (WST) is not fully freely convertible outside Samoa. Current account transactions for trade and services are generally permitted through authorized dealer banks with duly presented commercial documentation. Capital account items — including inbound equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, dividend distributions, liquidation proceeds, and other profit repatriation — require prior CBS exchange control approval or a valid standing exemption granted to International Companies under the Exchange Control (International Companies) Exemption Notice. For an offshore SaaS/vertical CRM operator, profit remittance is navigable through audited financial statements and board resolutions; the CBS scrutinises substance and source-of-income documentation to prevent circumvention of domestic taxation and laundering of overseas earnings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of goods and services from Samoa must obtain a valid exchange control approval for each export transaction. Export proceeds must be repatriated and offered for sale to an authorized dealer within 90 days from the date of export unless a CBS standing consent permits retention in a foreign currency account abroad. For an International Company exporting software-as-a-service subscriptions, the CBS generally grants standing permission to maintain offshore USD/AUD/NZD collection accounts where the underlying customer contracts are wholly non-resident and no conversion into WST is needed; if any proceeds are brought into Samoa, the mandatory conversion ratio is 100% into WST via an authorized dealer unless the foreign exchange approval explicitly permits a different split.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (foreign currency account) and Capital Escrow Sub-Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Samoa does not maintain a standalone electronic-money institution licensing regime for non-resident digital banks; offshore EMIs such as Stripe, Airwallex, and Mercury cannot directly settle into WST bank accounts without a domestic authorized dealer intermediary. These EMIs are viable for collecting subscription revenue in USD/EUR/AUD via card rails and for processing customer payouts, with periodic SWIFT sweeps to the Samoa IC bank account. Legal constraints include the foreign exchange approval obligation, the requirement to route any WST conversions through an authorized dealer, and CBS expectations regarding the traceability of cross-border payment flows. Therefore the recommended architecture is a hybrid: local Samoa bank account as the treasury anchor, with Stripe Billing as the front-end payment gateway and an accepted EMI aggregator only for short-dated settlement settlement corridors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners are generally required to undergo a physical KYC interview at the bank with the relationship officer; remote video opening may be permitted only for established white-list jurisdictions and on a case-by-case basis under CBS AML/CFT guidelines. For a Samoan International Company with no local operations and non-resident shareholders, the bank will insist that at least one authorised signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner attend an in-person or notarized remote interview, and that the licensed registered agent in Samoa present certified corporate registers, board resolutions, and the original Certificate of Incorporation. If no physical appearance is possible, the bank may decline the file unless an approved digital onboarding waiver is obtained with enhanced due diligence, third-party compliance opinions, and confirmation from the registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical business presence, employees, or substantive operations in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office certificate issued by the licensed agent; agent attestation of client due diligence; board resolution explaining the offshore ERP/cloud business model; audited financial statements of the IC or group entities; legal opinion from Samoan counsel on compliance with the International Companies Act; reference letter from the overseas parent or principal bank showing positive conduct.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Traditional Chinese family trust, nominee shareholder, or complex discretionary trust structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the trust deed (or settlor and trustee statements if discretionary); full identification of settlor, protector, beneficiaries, and trustee; notarized passports and proof of residential address; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; independent legal tax advice confirming no bearer-share or nominee concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear register of members, potential bearer instruments, or historical restructuring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete register of members certified by the registered agent; share allotment resolutions; share certificates; signed statutory declaration from each director confirming that the International Company issued no bearer shares and that all transfers are registered in the Samoa International Companies Register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS revenue with multiple merchant gateways and fragmented subscription sources
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying customer contracts and invoices; Stripe Billing payout and reconciliation statements; monthly foreign currency receivables ledger; transaction histories from all payment gateways; directors' explanation of revenue generation and obligation flows; on-demand audit pack prepared by the external accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound share capital into the Samoa International Company: (i) execute a directors' board resolution resolving to issue shares to the overseas investor; (ii) remit the contribution by SWIFT from the investor's bank using MT103/MT202, with the beneficiary field identifying the Samoan bank and the account reference 'WS IC Capital Escrow Account'; (iii) include in the remittance narrative the inward investment purpose code, e.g. 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — INTERNATIONAL COMPANY INCORPORATION NO. [...]', plus the unique reference of the exchange control approval; (iv) deliver to the Samoan bank a completed CBS foreign exchange declaration, certified board resolution, share application, and COP of the investor's board sanction; (v) the receiving bank will verify the reconciliation with the capital escrow credit and issue an inward foreign exchange certificate before share certificates are issued. For shareholder loans, the loan agreement, interest-rate schedule, and repayment plan must accompany the remittance to ensure the credit is classified as external financial liability rather than equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for software license fees, partner commissions, infrastructure purchases, and vendor payments are executed through the Samoa bank's SWIFT network. Routine operational disbursements use MT103 with full invoice referencing and must be supported by a current corporate resolution listing authorised signatories. Large-value infrastructure procurement may be effected through a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) advised via the Samoan bank's correspondent in New York or Sydney, with SWIFT MT700 issuance and MT754 acknowledgements; funds are released against presentation of complying shipping and intellectual-property delivery documents. The underlying clearing rails for USD and AUD are correspondent accounts maintained with tier-1 clearing banks overseas, as Samoa does not operate real-time foreign-currency gross settlement. For transactions above CBS-monitored thresholds, submission of an exchange control application with invoice, contract, and transmittal evidence is mandatory before value date.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts with an authorized dealer in Samoa, strictly for a bona fide underlying commercial exposure (receivables/payables) and with matching maturity tenure
Back-to-back multi-currency cash sweeps and natural hedging via multi-currency Nostro accounts, which avoid derivatives and comply with CBS current-account approvals
Short-dated currency swaps using USD/AUD towards WST where both legs arise from identifiable trade transactions and prior CBS exchange control approval has been issued

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June; first filing due by 30 June of the year following incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs penalty of 10% of the annual fee plus interest at 10% per annum; continued non-filing for 3 months after the due date may trigger administrative strike-off and forfeiture of the company's assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Annual Return, on or before 30 June; any shareholding or UBO change must be notified within 14 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation constitutes an offence under the International Companies Act; liable to fines and potential deregistration of the International Company

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for a typical private International Company; compulsory audit is triggered only if the company makes a public offer of securities, becomes a licensed financial institution, or is directed by the Registrar of International Companies
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted in Samoa; International Companies may maintain accounting records in any currency and are generally not required to file financial statements with the Registrar

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must submit an annual confirmation of the beneficial ownership register to the Registrar; all transfers of shares and resulting UBO changes must be updated in the register and notified within 14 days of the transaction
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (International Company fully exempt under the International Companies Act 1987; standard Samoa resident company headline rate is 27%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from Samoa income tax, value-added goods and services tax (VAGST), stamp duty and exchange control; offshore ERP/CRM cloud subscription revenue, software licence fees and related service income earned by an International Company is not subject to Samoa taxation; no capital gains tax on disposal of IC shares or IP assets; no branch profit tax imposed on non-resident beneficial owners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CI-01 (Annual Income Tax Return for Companies) filed through the Samoa Ministry of Revenue online e-Services portal; tax-exempt International Companies alternatively file Form CI-EX (Exemption Declaration) supported by the IC registration certificate issued under the International Companies Act 1987.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; Samoa's fiscal year is the calendar year (1 January to 31 December), so the annual return deadline is 30 June of the following year. Provisional tax instalments, where applicable, are payable quarterly on 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer Registration Number (TRN) and business registration number; for an International Company, quote the IC number issued by the Registrar of International Companies and full registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Samoa-registered agent's TRN and address; the non-resident beneficial owner is identified by legal name and country of residence in the supplementary schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the income year; standard 12-month period normally aligned with the calendar year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the financial year used in the IC's accounting records; a change of year-end requires prior written approval of the Commissioner of Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income derived from Samoa-source activities, including software licence fees, cloud subscriptions, CRM service revenue, interest and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an exempt IC, enter zero where all income is validly offshore-sourced; attach a schedule of revenue by customer jurisdiction and payment rail (Stripe Billing or Direct Debit) to substantiate non-Samoa sourcing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income exempted under section 36 of the International Companies Act 1987 or specific income tax legislation provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full amount of offshore vertical ERP/CRM subscription income and attach the IC exemption certificate; failure to substantiate the exemption recharacterises the income as taxable Box 3 income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred in deriving assessable income: cloud infrastructure, developer salaries, commissions, marketing, depreciation and amortisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where income is fully exempt, no deductions may be claimed; where a mixed-source position exists, apportion deductions strictly on an arm's length basis under transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income minus allowable deductions; the base on which the corporate income tax rate is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a fully exempt IC, enter zero; a non-resident IC is in any event taxable only on Samoa-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax at the applicable rate, net of foreign tax credits and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter nil for a tax-exempt IC; foreign tax credits are unavailable on exempt income and cannot be refunded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of a director or the registered agent, plus certification by a licensed tax advisor where relevant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent signs on behalf of the non-resident board; the agent remains liable for filing truthfulness and may incur fines for incorrect declarations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the assessed tax (minimum WST 200) for the first month and 2% for each additional month or part thereof, capped at 25%; persistent non-filing attracts a daily default penalty of WST 50 per day and an offence fine up to WST 100,000; directors and the registered agent face personal civil recovery for the penalties. A tax-exempt IC that fails to file the Registrar's annual return suffers a WST 50 per day default penalty and strike-off after two consecutive years of default.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company; profits of an IC are exempt from Samoa tax and distributions to non-resident shareholders are free of withholding tax. A statutory non-resident dividend withholding rate of 15% applies only to resident companies paying dividends to non-residents, subject to treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's double taxation agreement (DTA) network applies only to taxes covered by each treaty. A non-resident shareholder claiming a reduced rate must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the treaty-partner revenue authority, complete the Samoa Ministry of Revenue Form RR-1 (Reduced Rate / Exemption Claim) and deliver it to the registered agent or Samoa paying entity before the distribution date; the payer must retain the TRC and supporting documents for 7 years. Where no DTA exists, the statutory rate applies and no relief is available.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding tax: 15% on royalties and 15% on interest where the payer is a Samoa-resident person; treaty rates generally reduce withholding to 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, with a possible 5% rate for royalties paid to a company that is the beneficial owner and resident of the other contracting state. An International Company licensing software from a non-resident is not obliged to withhold when it pays no Samoa tax and all flows are offshore, but it must nevertheless document the beneficial owner to satisfy AML and economic substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa does not publish a specific WST-denominated Local File threshold for International Companies; the Commissioner of Revenue may require a transfer pricing study where related-party revenue exceeds WST 1,000,000 in a tax year or where the IC conducts controlled transactions with a Samoa-resident connected person regardless of amount. Prudent compliance practice: prepare a Local File when annual related-party turnover reaches WST 1,000,000 and a Master File when consolidated group turnover exceeds WST 5,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), adopted in 2019 under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Rules, apply to International Companies carrying on relevant activities, expressly including distribution and service businesses, holding companies, and intellectual property holding, which covers vertical ERP/CRM software licensing. The IC must demonstrate in Samoa: board meetings and minutes, a physical office or premises, full-time employees appropriate to the ERP/CRM activity, and active decision-making from Samoa. Non-compliant ICs are struck off, their annual certificate is refused, and directors and the registered agent are liable to fines up to WST 100,000 plus disqualification orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Offshore Tax Evasion / False Exemption Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Marketing or administering the IC as a zero-tax vehicle while the enterprise actually renders ERP/CRM services to Samoa-resident customers, accepts Samoa-sourced subscription revenue through Stripe Billing or Direct Debit, and conceals that income by filing a nil return or exemption declaration without disclosing the Samoa-source receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty equal to 100% of the tax avoided, plus a late payment penalty of 10% and an incremental late payment penalty of 2% per month thereafter; criminal fine up to WST 300,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years for the entity and its controlling officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil restitution for taxes, penalties and interest jointly and severally; the court may pierce the IC's veil and order directors to reimburse the company for the entire loss; directors on a non-resident board face travel bans, refusal of entry into Samoa, and extradition risk from treaty-partner states for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding the enterprise's ERP/CRM software IP and collecting royalty or subscription income in an IC with no premises, employees, or board control in Samoa; the arrangement lacks genuine substance and is abused solely to avoid residence-country taxation of the vertical cloud business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the IC tax exemption with assessment at 27% on deemed Samoa-source income; ESR non-compliance penalty of WST 20,000 per failure; strike-off of the company and forfeiture of the IP assets registered in its name.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered agent are jointly liable for unpaid corporate tax up to WST 500,000; a director who signs a false economic substance declaration commits an offence carrying up to 5 years' imprisonment and automatic disqualification from acting as a director of any Samoa company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing fraudulent or high-risk subscription payments through the IC's Stripe Billing account, accepting funds from sanctioned persons or jurisdictions, or failing to conduct customer due diligence on the CRM client base despite the Low_Risk_Standard banking tier designation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018, fines up to WST 1,000,000 for the entity; the registered agent's licence may be revoked; the IC becomes subject to a mandatory AML compliance audit and its bank accounts may be frozen by the Central Bank of Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit the laundering of criminal proceeds are liable to imprisonment up to 10 years and personal asset confiscation orders; directors also face international banking blacklists, travel bans in Samoa and treaty jurisdictions, and disqualification from professional office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Dividend Distribution / Insolvent Winding Up
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and paying dividends out of the IC's exempt profits while the company is insolvent, while outstanding payroll taxes, VAGST or arm's length liabilities to the operating ERP/CRM subsidiary remain unpaid, or stripping the vehicle without performing proper solvency tests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The distribution is voidable and recoverable from shareholders; the company is liable to a civil penalty of three times the unlawful distribution amount; the Registrar may place the IC into compulsory winding up and assets may be seized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised the distribution are personally liable to compensate creditors without limitation; the court may order repatriation of funds from foreign accounts, impose a 3-year travel ban, and commit disobedient directors to imprisonment for contempt.
